raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

MoRIIO gives two workers the same handshake and notify port when an instance has both TP > 1 and DP > 1, so a TP2 x DP2 prefill hangs at startup. This PR computes every port offset with the TP size of the instance that owns the port.

## Claims

- A MoRIIO instance with TP > 1 and DP > 1 (here prefill TP2 x DP2 x EP4) starts and serves requests. Before this change, prefill hung at startup with `ZMQError: Address already in use (addr='tcp://*:6302')`.
- Every worker of a TP x DP instance gets a unique notify port and handshake port, and the WRITE allocation and release notifications reach the right prefill rank.
- Port numbers do not change when TP = 1 or DP = 1, so existing deployments are not affected.

## Validation

**Unit tests.** Two cases fail on `main` and pass with this change:
- `test_notify_ports_are_unique_across_tp_and_dp_ranks`: the listener side.
- A new `remote_dp_rank=1` case in `test_release_reaches_every_prefill_rank_and_no_other`: the sender side.

```
# main (4e0ad5720)
$ python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_write_done_routing.py \
    -k "notify_ports_are_unique or release_reaches_every_prefill_rank"
E       assert [61005, 61006, 61006, 61007] == [61005, 61006, 61007, 61008]
E       AssertionError: assert [('tA', '10.0....0.1', 20002)] == [('tA', '10.0....0.1', 20003)]
2 failed, 3 passed

# this PR
$ python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_*.py
874 passed
```

These ran on MI350X in `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm72-edad8b03c` with this branch's source tree mounted. MoRIIO and the toy proxy are identical between that image's commit and `main` 4e0ad5720.

**End to end** (MI350X, GPT-OSS-120B, MoRIIO WRITE over XGMI, the toy proxy):
- Prefill: TP2 x DP2 x EP4 on 4 GPUs.
- Decode: TP1 on 1 GPU.
- Workload: 4 requests of 8,167 input tokens each and 1,024 output tokens, temperature 0.

| | prefill startup | notify ports bound | requests |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main | hangs: `Address already in use (tcp://*:6302)`, then "No available shared memory broadcast block found" every 60 s | 6302 twice | none served |
| this PR | ready in 170 s | 61005, 61006, 61007, 61008 | 4/4 succeed on both prefill DP ranks, coherent outputs |

The end-to-end run also needed two fixes that are not part of this PR:
- **The toy proxy pins the decode leg to the prefill DP rank.** With DP1 decode, that fails with `data_parallel_rank 1 is out of range [0, 1)`. That's a separate fix.
- **mori `WaitAll` on XGMI returns only at `transfer_timeout`.** That added ~30 s to TTFT. Separate issue, not fixed here.

The same port fix, applied as a local patch, also served a full 8K-in / 1K-out sweep at concurrency 1-128 (1,020 requests) on this 4:1 layout with no errors.

## Details

**Root cause.** Each MoRIIO worker binds its handshake and notify sockets at `base + get_port_offset(dp_rank, tp_rank, tp_size)`, and its peers have to compute the same number to reach it. `tp_size` defaulted to 1, and the call sites disagreed:

| side | call site | offset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| notify listener | `MoRIIOConfig.from_vllm_config` | `dp + tp` |
| handshake listener | `MoRIIOConnectorWorker.__init__` (`side_channel_port`) | `dp + tp` |
| WRITE alloc notify / release to prefill | `update_state_after_alloc`, `_release_write_prefill_blocks` | `dp + tp` |
| WRITE `write_done` to decode | `MoRIIOWriter._resolve_notify_endpoint` | `dp + tp` |
| handshake dial | `_moriio_handshake` | `dp * tp_size + tp` |
| READ release | `_read_blocks` | `dp * tp_size + tp` |

With TP2 x DP2, `dp + tp` gives offset 1 to both (dp0, tp1) and (dp1, tp0), so the second bind fails. That kills its listener thread, and the engine hangs in the first collective.

**Fix.** Make `tp_size` a required argument and pass the TP size of the instance that owns the port at every call site:
- Listeners pass their own TP size.
- Senders pass the peer's TP size: `get_moriio_peer_tp_size` for prefill, `WriteTask.remote_tp_size` for decode.
- When the peer's TP size is unknown, senders fall back to the local TP size, which is the existing "unknown means homogeneous" convention.

Making the argument required means a future call site can't silently fall back to `dp + tp`.

**Compatibility.** Offsets only change when TP > 1 and DP > 1, and that setup could not start before. Prefill and decode instances must run a vLLM version that both have this fix, which is already required for the other MoRIIO TP x DP changes.

**Not a duplicate.** I searched open PRs and issues for MoRIIO port, `get_port_offset`, handshake port and TP/DP. #58435, #39276 and #38813 edit lines next to two of these call sites, but they keep the two-argument `get_port_offset(dp, tp)`, so none of them fixes the mismatch. Whichever lands second may need a trivial rebase.

**Tests.** The existing tests in `test_moriio_write_done_routing.py` computed their expected ports with `get_port_offset(dp, tp)`, so they encoded the mismatch. They now pass the owner's TP size. The new listener test builds a real `VllmConfig` and patches only the TP rank and size, because a real TP2 rank needs two GPUs.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to find the bug, write the change and run the validation above.

Independent SMG validation of the unchanged production fix at head `4e123050ee6ff2a8c86ccf678735380ad87eea6f`: **PASS for two single-pod DP2 + heterogeneous-TP WRITE configurations**.

| Job | Model / precision | Prefill | Decode | Transport |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 51973 | Qwen3-30B-A3B, GQA / bf16 | DP2 × TP2, EP4 | DP2 × TP1, EP2 | Single-node XGMI |
| 51981 | Same fixed model revision | DP2 × TP1, EP2 | DP2 × TP2, EP4 | Two-node RDMA |

Each run used SMG's clean `003fa53f2bcfc987c7dd0716f48d910b3eb2e4bc` CI build and an actual ROCm7.2 engine at `df6603f0583375f244d1ac6d36265462b7490392` (already containing merged #61726), OCI digest `sha256:c26b8955052a9fc5b5437bd90eb8733b2e8f6f4308a95c7ff2db863aa192a777`. Only this PR's unchanged production diff was cleanly applied to its three connector files; four other connector files, 36 serving native objects and 12 distribution metadata files retained their frozen identities. Model revision: `ad44e777bcd18fa416d9da3bd8f70d33ebb85d39`. Both legs used block size16, eager bf16, matching DP2 and sequential WRITE dispatch; expert all-to-all was `allgather_reducescatter`.

For **each** run: all distributed worker identities were verified; four routed serial requests matched direct-prefill references and used the same P/D ranks **0,1,0,1**. Eight more routed requests at client concurrency four returned HTTP200, eight own nonces and no foreign nonces. Decode external KV exactly equalled raw response prompt usage, with observed zero local-compute and local-cache-hit tokens:

- 51973: **38,737 tokens**; concurrent P/D engine totals **12,889 / 12,880**.
- 51981: **38,384 tokens**; concurrent P/D engine totals **13,049 / 12,708**. Its four serial and one batch NIC windows independently had **P TX = D RX = full padded KV payload** (3,779,592,192 bytes total), with references outside the windows.

The actual upstream test file ran **30 passed, no failures/errors/skips in each of the three containers** (90 test executions: the same 30 cases in three containers). Separately, our CPU contract reproduced five of six failures on the unpatched source and six of six passing after this exact fix. This is additional SMG evidence, separate from the PR author's toy-proxy results. No unpatched-GPU A/B claim is made.

These were explicit derivative environments: private Cairo/Pycairo dependencies and a missing MI355X name-table entry. RDMA additionally required one fixed Ionic provider ELF for the cluster's kernel ABI; the actual pristine provider failed to enumerate devices, the replacement opened all eight devices per node, and non-provider loaded/resolved dependency hashes stayed unchanged. The original serving-native and distribution-metadata gates remained in force. Actual strict pip checks and all Slurm terminal exits passed; the job-owned directories were removed and independently checked.

The results support this single-pod, equal-DP port fix in both stated TP directions. They do not validate unequal DP, multi-pod prefix-hit release, concurrent leg dispatch or abort/restart reclamation; those remain separate. In particular this is not a claim that the PR has merged or that same-node small-P / large-D XGMI is supported.

(AI-assisted.)

Additional downstream source-compatibility checks are complete for the unchanged production patch in this PR. The three MoRI source files at main `bf45b38f0d68511f571b85f1a716997978647b28` match the audited `32a4dbfd` files: the patch applies cleanly after #64330. After applying the patch in a private source copy, all seven port-offset calls pass the owner's TP size explicitly, and the new completion-wait function is preserved exactly. Syntax checks pass for all three files before and after applying the patch. This is source compatibility, rather than a runtime validation of the newer main.

The existing downstream SMG 1.13.0 evidence and redacted logs are in [the earlier validation comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64574#issuecomment-6567743569): equal-DP2 small-prefill-TP1 to larger-decode-TP2 WRITE/RDMA, plus the reverse TP2-to-TP1 WRITE/XGMI actual pytest. Those runs retain their documented source, hardware and environment boundaries.

The old pre-run failures in [run 40953014053](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/40953014053) and [run 40953103643](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/40953103643) stop at the label/author-history eligibility step, before source checkout or pre-commit. That condition is separate from Draft state; these attempts do not report a source-format or test failure. Further CI follows the repository's maintainer trust policy.

🚀

Independent SMG validation of the unchanged production fix at head `4e123050ee6ff2a8c86ccf678735380ad87eea6f`: **PASS for two single-pod DP2 + heterogeneous-TP WRITE configurations**.

| Job | Model / precision | Prefill | Decode | Transport |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 51973 | Qwen3-30B-A3B, GQA / bf16 | DP2 × TP2, EP4 | DP2 × TP1, EP2 | Single-node XGMI |
| 51981 | Same fixed model revision | DP2 × TP1, EP2 | DP2 × TP2, EP4 | Two-node RDMA |

Each run used SMG's clean `003fa53f2bcfc987c7dd0716f48d910b3eb2e4bc` CI build and an actual ROCm7.2 engine at `df6603f0583375f244d1ac6d36265462b7490392` (already containing merged #61726), OCI digest `sha256:c26b8955052a9fc5b5437bd90eb8733b2e8f6f4308a95c7ff2db863aa192a777`. Only this PR's unchanged production diff was cleanly applied to its three connector files; four other connector files, 36 serving native objects and 12 distribution metadata files retained their frozen identities. Model revision: `ad44e777bcd18fa416d9da3bd8f70d33ebb85d39`. Both legs used block size16, eager bf16, matching DP2 and sequential WRITE dispatch; expert all-to-all was `allgather_reducescatter`.

For **each** run: all distributed worker identities were verified; four routed serial requests matched direct-prefill references and used the same P/D ranks **0,1,0,1**. Eight more routed requests at client concurrency four returned HTTP200, eight own nonces and no foreign nonces. Decode external KV exactly equalled raw response prompt usage, with observed zero local-compute and local-cache-hit tokens:

- 51973: **38,737 tokens**; concurrent P/D engine totals **12,889 / 12,880**.
- 51981: **38,384 tokens**; concurrent P/D engine totals **13,049 / 12,708**. Its four serial and one batch NIC windows independently had **P TX = D RX = full padded KV payload** (3,779,592,192 bytes total), with references outside the windows.

The actual upstream test file ran **30 passed, no failures/errors/skips in each of the three containers** (90 test executions: the same 30 cases in three containers). Separately, our CPU contract reproduced five of six failures on the unpatched source and six of six passing after this exact fix. This is additional SMG evidence, separate from the PR author's toy-proxy results. No unpatched-GPU A/B claim is made.

These were explicit derivative environments: private Cairo/Pycairo dependencies and a missing MI355X name-table entry. RDMA additionally required one fixed Ionic provider ELF for the cluster's kernel ABI; the actual pristine provider failed to enumerate devices, the replacement opened all eight devices per node, and non-provider loaded/resolved dependency hashes stayed unchanged. The original serving-native and distribution-metadata gates remained in force. Actual strict pip checks and all Slurm terminal exits passed; the job-owned directories were removed and independently checked.

The results support this single-pod, equal-DP port fix in both stated TP directions. They do not validate unequal DP, multi-pod prefix-hit release, concurrent leg dispatch or abort/restart reclamation; those remain separate. In particular this is not a claim that the PR has merged or that same-node small-P / large-D XGMI is supported.

(AI-assisted.)

Additional downstream source-compatibility checks are complete for the unchanged production patch in this PR. The three MoRI source files at main `bf45b38f0d68511f571b85f1a716997978647b28` match the audited `32a4dbfd` files: the patch applies cleanly after #64330. After applying the patch in a private source copy, all seven port-offset calls pass the owner's TP size explicitly, and the new completion-wait function is preserved exactly. Syntax checks pass for all three files before and after applying the patch. This is source compatibility, rather than a runtime validation of the newer main.

The existing downstream SMG 1.13.0 evidence and redacted logs are in [the earlier validation comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64574#issuecomment-6567743569): equal-DP2 small-prefill-TP1 to larger-decode-TP2 WRITE/RDMA, plus the reverse TP2-to-TP1 WRITE/XGMI actual pytest. Those runs retain their documented source, hardware and environment boundaries.

The old pre-run failures in [run 40953014053](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/40953014053) and [run 40953103643](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/40953103643) stop at the label/author-history eligibility step, before source checkout or pre-commit. That condition is separate from Draft state; these attempts do not report a source-format or test failure. Further CI follows the repository's maintainer trust policy.

If there are remaining implementation or validation tasks before this can be marked Ready for review, please identify them so we can help with a focused follow-up.
